answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent checks show the agent fabricated results or colluded. Reputation and access limits attach to the stake-backed account, so splitting into many names does not multiply influence; each new identity must lock fresh capital and wait through review. The rule does not prove a personhood uniqueness—raven, willow, and ferrous are just names—but it makes a Sybil campaign costly: the attacker ties up funds and risks losing them for each account.
